plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before leaves emerge. Widely cultivated in East Asia for ornamental use and for its sour fruit, which is pickled or made into liqueur.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Japan, China, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are traditionally celebrated in Japan before cherry blossoms, and in Chinese culture the plum is one of the 'Three Friends of Winter' for its resilience in cold weather.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals. It grows in woodlands and meadows and is the ancestor of many cultivated daffodil varieties.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to April)
plants.location: Western Europe, including England, Wales, France, and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: Daffodil bulbs contain lycorine and other alkaloids that make them toxic, which is why rodents and deer usually leave them alone. Galantamine, a compound from related plants, is used in Alzheimer's medication.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A large tree from the Himalayas that bears huge, goblet-shaped flowers on bare branches in late winter. The blooms can reach 25 cm across and make a dramatic display in mild-climate gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to April)
plants.location: Eastern Himalayas (Nepal, Bhutan, northeast India, southwest China); cultivated in mild gardens in the UK, New Zealand, and the US Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: A Campbell's magnolia can take 20 to 30 years from seed to produce its first flowers, and magnolias belong to one of the oldest flowering plant lineages, predating bees.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: A bulbous perennial from South Africa that sends up leafless stalks topped with clusters of fragrant, trumpet-shaped pink flowers. Leaves appear after flowering finishes, which gives it the name 'naked lady'.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn in the Southern Hemisphere (February to April)
plants.location: Western Cape, South Africa; naturalized in Australia, California, and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: Its flower stalks emerge suddenly after summer heat or rain, and it is the only species in the genus Amaryllis. The large red 'amaryllis' sold at Christmas is actually a Hippeastrum.
